questions.prompt: You have {m:1400} in Spend. You buy a book for {m:550}. How much is left?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That adds the two amounts. Buying takes money away.
Not quite. That's the price of the book. What's left after paying it?

questions.wrong: Not quite. Take the price away from what you have.
hints: Start with {m:1400} and take away the price.
{m:1400} take away {m:500} is {m:900}. Now take away {m:50} more.
questions.correct: That's it. {m:850} is left in Spend.

questions.prompt: You get {m:1000} and put {m:400} in Save. How much goes to Spend?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That adds the two. Save is part of the {m:1000}, so take it away.
Not quite. That's the Save part. What's left for Spend?

questions.wrong: Not quite. Spend gets whatever doesn't go to Save.

questions.prompt: A goal costs {m:2200}. You start from zero and save {m:500} a week. How many weeks will it take?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. 4 weeks gives {m:2000}. That's {m:200} short, so round up to the next week.

questions.wrong: Not quite. See how many weeks of {m:500} it takes to reach {m:2200}.
hints: 4 weeks gives {m:2000}. Is that enough for {m:2200}?
questions.correct: That's it. 5 weeks. After 4 weeks you're {m:200} short, so you round up.

questions.prompt: You have {m:1200} and choose a game for {m:800}. What can you no longer get as well?

options.feedback: Yes. After the game you have {m:400}, and the book costs {m:600}.
Not quite. After the game you have {m:400}, so the snack still fits.
Not quite. The game uses {m:800}, so some things no longer fit.

hints: Work out what's left after the game.
{m:400} is left. Which of these costs more than that?
questions.correct: Nice. That's it. Choosing the game means giving up the book, for now.

questions.prompt: You save {m:300} a week for a goal. Your weekly saving drops to {m:200}. What happens to your plan?

options.feedback: Yes. Less each week means more weeks to reach the same price.
Not quite. Less going into Save each week means it takes longer.
Not quite. Saving less each week can't get you there sooner.

hints: Less goes in each week. What does that do?
Smaller weekly steps take more steps to reach the same price.
questions.correct: Right. Saving less each week means more weeks to reach the goal.
